classification.difficultyReason: Select the relevant triangles and RHS or SAS, then connect matching angles to parallelism or combine equal adjacent angles with their supplementary sum. The linked proofs use the supplied diagrams and taught procedures.

spec.description: Opposite right triangles at N; A,N,D and B,N,C are collinear. Matching double ticks on AB and CD, single ticks on BN and NC, and a right-angle square in ANB. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.answerVisibility: All givens remain visible; no inferred equal angles or parallel marks are supplied.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}AB&=DC &&\text{(given)}\\BN&=CN &&\text{(given)}\\\angle ANB&=\angle DNC=90^\circ &&\text{(vertically opposite angles)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle NAB\equiv\triangle NDC$ (RHS).

answer.short: $\angle NAB=\angle NDC$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).
answer.worked: Since $\triangle NAB\equiv\triangle NDC$, $\angle NAB=\angle NDC$ (matching angles of congruent triangles). Hence $\angle A=\angle D$.
$\angle NAB=\angle NDC$ are alternate angles formed by transversal $AD$. Therefore $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: Two right triangles share vertical PR. PQ and SR are horizontal. PS and QR have matching double ticks. Right-angle squares occur at P and R. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: PS=QR; angle QPR=angle SRP=90 degrees; PR is common.
spec.answerVisibility: No parallel arrows or inferred equal angles are added.

answer.worked: $\angle QPR=\angle SRP=90^\circ$ are alternate angles formed by transversal $PR$. Therefore $PQ\parallel SR$.

$$\begin{align*}PS&=RQ &&\text{(given)}\\PR&=RP &&\text{(common side)}\\\angle PRS&=\angle RPQ=90^\circ &&\text{(given)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle PRS\equiv\triangle RPQ$ (RHS).

answer.short: $PS\parallel QR$ because matching angles $\angle SPR=\angle QRP$ are alternate angles.
answer.worked: $\angle SPR=\angle QRP$ (matching angles of congruent triangles). These are alternate angles formed by transversal $PR$, so $PS\parallel QR$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use congruence to prove that $AB\parallel CD$, given that $O$ is the centre of the circle.

spec.description: Unshaded circle with red centre O, diameters AD and BC, and chords AB and CD. Ordinary source blue is rendered black; the highlighted centre uses standard red.
spec.mathematics: A,O,D are collinear; B,O,C are collinear; OA,OB,OC,OD are radii.
spec.answerVisibility: No inferred equal-length marks, angle marks or parallel arrows are supplied.

answer.short:
$AB\parallel CD$.

Use SAS to prove $\triangle AOB\equiv\triangle DOC$, then use equal alternate angles.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}OA&=OD &&\text{(radii)}\\OB&=OC &&\text{(radii)}\\\angle AOB&=\angle DOC &&\text{(vertically opposite angles)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle AOB\equiv\triangle DOC$ (SAS).

Hence $\angle ABO=\angle DCO$ (matching angles of congruent triangles). These are alternate angles formed by transversal $BC$, so $AB\parallel CD$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Prove that $\angle ABC=\angle ABD$ using congruence, and hence prove that $AB\perp CD$.

spec.description: Triangle ACD with B on CD, segment AB, matching double ticks on AC and AD, and alpha labels on both sides of AB at A. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: AC=AD; angle CAB=angle BAD=alpha; C,B,D are collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: No right-angle square is supplied: perpendicularity is to be proved.

answer.short:
$\angle ABC=\angle ABD=90^\circ$, so $AB\perp CD$.

Use SAS, matching angles and supplementary angles.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}AB&=AB &&\text{(common side)}\\AC&=AD &&\text{(given)}\\\angle BAC&=\angle BAD &&\text{(given)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle BAC\equiv\triangle BAD$ (SAS).

Hence $\angle ABC=\angle ABD$ (matching angles of congruent triangles). Since $C,B,D$ are collinear, these angles are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC+\angle ABD&=180^\circ\\2\angle ABC&=180^\circ\\\angle ABC&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$
Thus $\angle ABD=90^\circ$ and $AB\perp CD$.
